Read .csv Chromatogram from the BioRad NGC

Source: R/chrom_read.R
chrom_read_ngc.Rd

Each trace in an NGC export is recorded at its own volumes. The traces are combined into one row per volume of the first absorbance trace, and the other traces are interpolated onto those volumes.

Usage

chrom_read_ngc(file, skip = 1)

Arguments

file

File path to the .csv file.

skip

Number of lines to skip before begin reading. Usually 1 line.

Value

A chromatogram: a tibble with the run's metadata, see chrom_meta().

Columns

The readers all give one row per sampled point, with the columns the instrument recorded:

  • time, in seconds, when the instrument records it, and volume, in mL.

  • fraction, the fraction each row was collected into, or NA when it wasn't collected.

  • Absorbance, named after its wavelength in nm, such as a280, or uv when the instrument doesn't record the wavelength.

  • The other traces under standard names: conductivity, conductivity_percent, percent_b, pressure, flow and temperature.

fraction is a fraction vector and the absorbance columns are absorbance vectors, which record their wavelength and unit. The other columns are quantity vectors with the unit recorded in the file, such as s, mL, mS/cm, psi or MPa.

Examples

fl <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  "ngc_sec.csv",
  package = "chromr"
)

dat <- chrom_read_ngc(fl)
dat
